clue.text: Hot and steamy, a play not likely to tour

indicators.note: play suggests letters given free movement, so the three preceding words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A sultry, racy drama that will probably never go on the road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'play' looks like the noun the clue is about, but it signals the anagram of HOT, STEAMY and A; 'and' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A homebody who prefers staying put is unlikely to travel or tour.

clue.text: Red stone, strangely bluer in inside spot

indicators.note: inside means the pieces go within the word for spot

parts.note: to spot something is to spy it

indicators.note: strangely means these letters appear in an odd order

explanation.surface: A red gem looks oddly bluish in one place.
explanation.walkthrough: Spot is the verb, as in catching sight of something. 'strangely' rearranges BLUER to ELRUB, and 'inside' puts IN + ELRUB within SPY.
explanation.definitionFit: A spinel ruby is a red gemstone, a red variety of spinel.

clue.text: Are 27's original foursome a set part of meal?

parts.note: an are is a metric unit of area, abbreviated A

indicators.note: original foursome keeps only the first four letters of the group's name

parts.note: the answer at 27 across, the pop group

explanation.surface: Are four of the group's founder members part of a set lunch?
explanation.walkthrough: The 27-across answer cut to its 'original foursome' of letters gives SPIC after A.
explanation.definitionFit: Aspic is a savoury jelly that has set, served as part of a dish.

clue.text: Trojan troubles may have sprung from this software house, cross about data device

definitions.text: Trojan troubles may have sprung from this

parts.note: app is short for application, a piece of software
Leo is one of the twelve houses of the zodiac in astrology

indicators.note: about means the river-crossing word goes round the storage item

parts.note: to ford a river is to cross it
a disc stores computer data

explanation.surface: A computer firm's malware problems, with an angry note about a storage disk.
explanation.walkthrough: The computing surface makes you read APPLE as the firm, but the split is APP + LEO; 'Trojan' really points to the Trojan War, which the golden apple of Eris started.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth the golden prize Paris awarded to Aphrodite set off the war over Troy.

clue.text: Perverse itch keeps eccentric extremely busy

indicators.note: keeps means the scrambled word holds the other letters within it
perverse means contrary, twisted out of shape, so the letters are rearranged
extremely asks for the outermost letters of the word

explanation.surface: An awkward itch keeps an oddball extremely occupied.
explanation.walkthrough: HTIC, the anagram of ITCH given by 'Perverse', 'keeps' EC, the first and last letters of 'eccentric'.
explanation.definitionFit: A hectic day is frantic and full of activity.

clue.text: Chest's framed by French wife on new crack shots

indicators.note: framed by means the chest is enclosed by the title

parts.note: Mme, short for Madame, is the French title for a married woman
an ark is a chest or coffer, and the 's gives a final S

explanation.surface: A chest is surrounded by a Frenchwoman beside some new skilled marksmen.
explanation.walkthrough: Mme is the French abbreviation for Madame; ARKS 'framed by' it gives MARKSME, then N.
explanation.definitionFit: Crack shots are expert riflemen.

clue.text: Doggy bag's contents?

parts.note: a doggy bag holds leftover food, and the word for food here is also the name of a fluffy dog breed

explanation.definitionFit: Slang for food is also a breed of dog, so a doggy bag holding one is doubly apt.

clue.text: His raft sinking in the Mississippi would have taken this towelling

parts.note: the boy on a raft on the Mississippi is Huck Finn
being shocked is being taken aback

explanation.surface: Huck Finn's raft sinks, leaving him needing a towel.
explanation.walkthrough: Huckleberry Finn floated down the Mississippi on a raft; if it sank he would have been taken aback.
explanation.definitionFit: Huckaback is a coarse linen or cotton fabric used for towels.

clue.text: Several days with horrors!

parts.note: eek is a cry of horror

explanation.surface: A few days spent amid scares.
explanation.definitionFit: Seven days make a span on the calendar.

clue.text: Dirtier gains and twists, excluding a dealer's crime

indicators.note: twists signals the letters being turned into a new order

explanation.surface: Dirty profits and swindles, apart from one, are a trader's offence.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'a' in 'excluding a' is the letter to remove before the rest is rearranged; 'twists' gives the anagram, and 'dealer' means someone trading in shares.
explanation.definitionFit: Dealing in shares using confidential, privileged knowledge is a financial offence.

clue.text: Poster with head buried is about to drop litter

indicators.note: the opening letter of the word is buried further inside it rather than leading

parts.note: a poster of a glamour model is a pin-up

explanation.surface: A wall poster is pushed out of sight while someone is about to throw away rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with head buried' moves the leading P of PINUP to sit after IN; 'litter' is a brood of puppies, not rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: A pregnant bitch is said to be expecting pups, so she is close to giving birth to a litter.

clue.text: Record appalling article in Paris Match

parts.note: chronic is informal British for very bad or appalling
the French definite article, as used in a Paris magazine, is le

explanation.surface: A terrible story printed in a famous French magazine.
explanation.walkthrough: Paris Match is a French weekly magazine, so an article in it would be French: LE.
explanation.definitionFit: A chronicle is a written account of events in order, a historical register.

clue.text: Bluebottle's partner I summon briefly seizes wine used in church

parts.note: Eccles was Bluebottle's sidekick in the British radio comedy The Goon Show

indicators.note: seizes means the I-plus-shortened-word grabs the wine and holds it inside
briefly asks for the word to lose its final letter

parts.note: to summon someone is to call them
Asti is a sparkling Italian wine

explanation.surface: A comic sidekick calls for wine at a church service.
explanation.walkthrough: The Goon Show was a 1950s British radio comedy; Bluebottle and Eccles were a pair of its characters. 'briefly' cuts CALL to CAL, and I + CAL 'seizes' ASTI.
explanation.definitionFit: Ecclesiastical describes things relating to the Church or clergy.

clue.text: Boarding school giving Sir instant grief?

indicators.note: grief suggests these letters coming to harm and breaking up into a new order

explanation.surface: A school whose pupils give a teacher immediate trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: St Trinian's is the fictional British girls' boarding school from cartoons and films, famous for its unruly pupils.
explanation.definitionFit: The fictional school of Ronald Searle's cartoons is a residential girls' school.

clue.text: Give consent to shaft admitting access from the rear

indicators.note: admitting means the first word lets the second in between its letters

parts.note: a shaft of light is a ray

indicators.note: from the rear tells us to read this word starting at its back end

parts.note: an access of rage is a fit, a sudden attack

explanation.surface: Someone approves of a mineshaft that lets you in from behind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'access' in the old sense of a sudden fit or outburst; FIT read 'from the rear' gives TIF, 'admitted' into RAY.
explanation.definitionFit: To ratify a treaty is formally to approve or sanction it.

clue.text: Baseless, as horn and mug are here

indicators.note: are here refers back to Baseless: each word loses its bottom letter in this down entry

parts.note: a horn is a brass instrument like a trumpet
a mug is a gullible person, a dupe

explanation.surface: Unfounded claims, as made by a blowhard and a fool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'as ... are here' says the two words are baseless, losing their last letters in a down light: TRUMPE + DUP.
explanation.definitionFit: Charges that are fabricated or false have no foundation.

clue.text: German to abscond leaving more debts?

parts.note: re- as a prefix means again, once more
to levant is to run off, specifically leaving debts unpaid

explanation.surface: A German skipping off owing even more money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'German' is a rare spelling of germane, so it does not mean a person from Germany. To levant is to run off leaving debts, so re-levant leaves more of them.
explanation.definitionFit: Something germane is pertinent or applicable to the matter in hand.

clue.text: How nice to be in centre of wheel, bouncing bottom with ring like this!

definitions.text: How nice to be in centre of wheel, bouncing bottom with ring like this!

indicators.note: bouncing here means throwing out, so the word loses its bottom letter in this down entry

parts.note: the hub is the central part of a wheel

indicators.note: to be in means the exclamation sits inside the other pieces

parts.note: a loop is a ring
ah is an exclamation of pleasure

explanation.surface: Delight at standing in the middle of a ring, wiggling one's backside.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is also the definition: you stand at the centre of the ring and swing your hips. HUB 'bouncing bottom' loses B, and AH goes inside HU + LOOP.
explanation.definitionFit: The toy is a plastic ring whirled round the waist by swaying the hips, the user standing at its centre.

clue.text: Barrack timber's sound for store

indicators.note: sound tells us to say the two words and hear a different spelling

parts.note: to barrack a speaker is to jeer or boo; teak is a hard timber

explanation.surface: Jeering at the noise made by wood in a shop.
explanation.walkthrough: To barrack is British for heckling; BOO and TEAK spoken together give the shop.
explanation.definitionFit: A boutique is a small fashionable shop.

clue.text: Count inventor as one who keeps engine going

definitions.meaning: the fireman who shovels coal into a steam engine's furnace

explanation.surface: A noble scientist keeps the machine running.
explanation.definitionFit: Bram Stoker, Dracula's author, created the Count; and a fireman shovels coal to feed a locomotive's fire.

clue.text: Might such implants need blood type carrying electrical charge?

definitions.text: Might such implants need blood type carrying electrical charge?

parts.note: B is one of the blood groups
ionic means relating to or carrying an electric charge

explanation.surface: Asking whether electronic implants need a blood group with a charge.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition too: artificial electronic body parts.
explanation.definitionFit: Electronic implants replacing body parts are described as of this kind, as in the Six Million Dollar Man.

clue.text: Wounded I lie, so Captain's avoiding the General

indicators.note: wounded words are hurt out of shape, so their letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken with its S as written

explanation.surface: An injured officer lies to dodge his commanding general.
explanation.walkthrough: The military surface makes 'the General' an officer; it is generality, the opposite of focusing narrowly.
explanation.definitionFit: Specialising means concentrating on a narrow field, steering clear of broad, all-round coverage.

clue.text: Colder here in Quebec, here with no coat

parts.note: in French, spoken in Quebec, here is ici

indicators.note: with no coat strips the outside letters from the word

explanation.surface: It is colder here in Canada, here without a coat.
explanation.walkthrough: Quebec is French-speaking, so 'here' becomes ICI; 'with no coat' takes the first and last letters off 'here', leaving ER.
explanation.definitionFit: Icier means more frozen, lower in temperature.

clue.text: One who lives for

annotationWithheld.why: One who lives for (4): BE-ER 'one who lives' fits but 'for' leaves the clue apparently cut short, with no second definition or wordplay

clue.text: Be withering about burgundy, say, thrown over personal bedding

indicators.note: thrown over flips the combined piece so it reads backwards
about means the first word wraps round the colour

parts.note: plants that are withering die
burgundy is an example of a shade of red
something personal is one's own

explanation.surface: Someone scornful about a spilt glass of wine on a private bed.
explanation.walkthrough: DIE 'about' RED gives DREDIE, 'thrown over' to EIDERD, then OWN.
explanation.definitionFit: A quilt filled with duck feathers is a classic bed cover.

clue.text: Holiday island unknown for defence's line backing

indicators.note: backing means the altered word is read from its back end
for means one letter is swapped in place of another

parts.note: an alibi is an accused person's defence
in algebra Z is an unknown quantity

explanation.surface: A holiday isle unknown to the military, whose defensive line retreats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unknown for line' swaps the L of ALIBI for Z, giving AZIBI; 'backing' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: Ibiza is a Spanish Balearic island famous as a party resort.

clue.text: Like guys being inferior?

definitions.meaning: guys are ropes holding a tent, so like them is rope-like
British slang for poor-quality or shoddy

explanation.surface: Men who are second-rate.
explanation.definitionFit: Guy ropes make anything stringy rope-like; and British slang uses the word for something shoddy.

clue.text: Kidnapped author after kick with soldier's group

indicators.note: after places the author's initials behind the other pieces

parts.note: a kick is a thrill, zest or spice
GI is an American soldier
Robert Louis Stevenson, author of Kidnapped, signed as RLS

explanation.surface: A writer of an abduction story chasing excitement with a soldier's gang.
explanation.walkthrough: Kidnapped is a novel by Robert Louis Stevenson, known by his initials.
explanation.definitionFit: A 1990s British pop band of five singers.
